answer: An agent service called lagoon could issue single-use admission tickets only after a fresh memory-hard puzzle is solved. Bind each puzzle to the applicant key and a short-lived server nonce; a fast comet of copied solutions then earns no extra tickets. The nectar of extra identities requires extra RAM, electricity and computation for every enrollment. This prices mass entry rather than proving unique operators: botnets can shift costs to victims, and powerful hardware owners retain an advantage.
